The duplicate-and-edit flow is ready at **http://maker:4001** (please refresh). Let me guide you through it:

1. Paste a link you already have — try **`https://figma.com`** (it's in your samples) and click **Fetch details**. Instead of adding a copy, you'll get a warning telling you it's already saved and **where** it lives, with a button to **edit the saved bookmark** instead.
2. Click **"Edit the saved bookmark"** — the existing bookmark opens in the same form (title, note, tags) with an "Editing…" banner. Change the title or a tag and click **Update bookmark**. Notice **no second copy appears** — your existing one is updated in place.

One choice I made while building this that I'd like your reaction to, since it goes slightly beyond duplicates:

- Since editing an existing bookmark now exists, I also added a plain **"Edit"** button on each bookmark in the list, so you can revise a title, note, or tags any time — not only when you hit a duplicate. Please check whether having that always-available Edit is welcome, or whether you'd rather editing only appear in the duplicate situation.

After trying it: **does the duplicate warning — and being guided to edit the existing bookmark — work the way you asked for?**
